title: list door: the paged list's count(*) stops dominating once indexes land — measure and offer a cheaper total (epic #33631 R12)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance). Item R12 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281 (corrected 6889939163). Maintainer's pick (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:44Z): 「R1 R7 R12 各一张+测量卡」.

## Today

Every paged list also runs `count(*)` with the full predicate (`protocol-data-crud.ts` ~803; `$count=false` already opts out). Member read-scoped total: PG 35 ms vs the page's 118 ms today; once #33695 lands the page is ~3 ms and the total becomes the dominant cost.

## Target

Decide per surface: the Console sends `$count=false` where it does not show a total, and/or the door answers a cheaper total (e.g. capped / estimated count) where the UI needs only "more than N". The PR measures both on the M0 bench after #33695.

## Business reason

After the index work, list latency is mostly the total count; most list views do not need an exact total.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area E1 (list door) with the UI lane for the Console call sites; next account; size S. Blocked-by: #33695 (its measurement is meaningful only after the index lands).

## Epic rules

- Name the SQL shape produced and give before/after on the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662).
- Security never regresses: read scope and tenant wall stay in the pushed-down statement, with a parity test against today's path.
- A non-SQL driver keeps an in-process path it already has or refuses with a stable code (epic #33631 rules; #33626 rulings).
